units.passage: Be wary of claims by third-party vendors. Familiarize yourself with the practices of these vendors before adopting such tools in your courses.
units.why: "Be wary of claims by third-party vendors" asks instructors to evaluate vendor tools before adopting them, P117.

units.passage: If you're teaching with a tool that does require students to create a third-party account, you must consider the security, accessibility, and cost of these tools, and provide the possibility to opt out.
units.policy: Instructors teaching with a tool that requires a third-party account must consider its security, accessibility, and cost
units.why: "you must consider the security, accessibility, and cost of these tools" binds instructors who choose third-party-account tools; it is about evaluating a tool before choosing it (P117), covering privacy, access and cost.
units.fit_note: Also names accessibility and cost, which P117 does not.

units.passage: Before using any AI platform, take the time to understand how it works, what data it collects, and how it handles that data.
units.policy: Before using any AI platform, users take the time to understand how it works, what data it collects, and how it handles that data
units.why: "Before using any AI platform, take the time to understand how it works, what data it collects, and how it handles that data" asks users to evaluate a tool before use; P117, should.

units.passage: Before using any AI service, review its current privacy, data-retention, model-training, security, and acceptable-use terms.
units.why: "Before using any AI service, review its current privacy, data-retention, model-training, security, and acceptable-use terms" tells users to assess a tool before use. P117 (evaluate a tool) fits best; P65 is institutional review. Consensus codes: actor=all, phase=during-work, modality=should, policy_type=P117, unit_stance=neutral.
units.fit_note: The evaluation concerns terms of service and data handling, not accuracy or fit to the task.

units.passage: Not all AI services are the same. Some have unclear data retention or training practices. Before committing to a tool for university work, understand how it handles your data.
units.why: 'Before committing to a tool for university work, understand how it handles your data' tells users to research a tool before choosing it: P117 (evaluate a tool), not P65, which is institutional review.

units.passage: always verify that the specific tool you are using is appropriate for your data.
units.why: "always verify that the specific tool you are using is appropriate" is assessing a tool's fit before use, P117.

units.passage: An evaluation tool that that prompts users to consider questions related to a tool's reliability, objective, bias, ownership, type.
units.policy: The guide offers the AI ROBOT Test, an evaluation tool that prompts users to consider a tool's reliability, objective, bias, ownership and type.
units.why: The AI ROBOT Test is described as prompting users 'to consider questions related to a tool's reliability, objective, bias, ownership, type', helping users evaluate a tool before choosing it (P117).

units.passage: Confirm that Gen AI resources that you suggest or require for your courses are not biased, prejudiced, or inaccurate in the information they produce.
units.why: "Confirm that Gen AI resources that you suggest or require ... are not biased, prejudiced, or inaccurate" asks instructors to vet tools before recommending them; nearest P117.
units.fit_note: Vetting is for bias and accuracy in tools instructors suggest or require.

units.passage: Learn the terms of service and privacy policies for the public Generative AI system you want to use.
units.why: "Learn the terms of service and privacy policies for the public Generative AI system you want to use" asks users to evaluate a tool before use; nearest P117.
units.fit_note: Evaluation is of terms of service and data handling, not accuracy or task fit. Focuses on terms and data handling rather than accuracy or task fit.

units.passage: For uses of generative AI that are not prohibited, UW–‍Madison faculty, staff, students and affiliates can help protect themselves and others by choosing tools and services that exhibit the National Institute of Standards and Technology’s (NIST’s) characteristics of trustworthy AI
units.why: "choosing tools and services that exhibit the National Institute of Standards and Technology’s (NIST’s) characteristics of trustworthy AI" asks users to pick trustworthy tools, P117.

units.passage: Research tools to better understand potential biases that may be present in their model or training data. Learn more about prompt engineering so you can better understand how your prompts affect potential outputs
units.why: "Research tools to better understand potential biases" asks users to assess tools before use; P117 (evaluate a tool) is closest, P53 does not fit since no harm is stated as a rule.
